cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Go of the Grudge
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender resentment, distance, or a claim that keeps the relationship stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your place beside mine for dinner. I missed your opening night, but I want us sitting together tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left my seat empty. You can have an empty one now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept the complaint, not the seating plan. Bring your plate over; you can be angry beside me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm still going to tell you every bit you missed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The floor is yours. Sit here and start with the first scene. I'm not asking you to pretend it didn't hurt; I'm asking you to stop eating it alone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets shared places, A3 accepts the complaint but rejects distancing seating and A5 grants the floor at A chosen side, using authority to persuade B to relinquish retaliatory distance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 empty-seat retaliation causes A3 distinction between anger and placement; B4 recounting condition causes A5 full listening permission.

relationship.evidence: B2 resentment follows a specific absence and B4 wants the missed performance heard, a credible route to less distance.

heightening.evidence: B4 demand to tell every missed part causes A5 to offer a sustained account beside A, not require emotional erasure.

specificity.evidence: A1 current dinner and missed opening establish the two seats; A5 first scene refers to B performance.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 complaint accepted but seating rejected gives status wit; A5 eating hurt alone is figurative and slightly strained.
